cluster_name: Shooting at Aarau techno rave kills woman, five injured
tldr: The headline layer across 22 outlets and 12 country buckets is almost entirely locked on a single CRIME_PUNISHMENT register: a fatal shooting at a Swiss rave with a manhunt underway for unknown perpetrators. No outlet raises political context, gun policy, or motive speculation at headline level — a strikingly narrow advertised frame that diverges from the fuller security-mobilisation and health-safety angles visible in body text. The principal variation at title level is register, not frame: roughly half the corpus leads with manhunt action ('Manhunt underway after…') while the other half leads with the event fact ('Shooting at rave… kills 1'). Two UK outlets (BBC World and Daily Mail) uniquely humanize the victim with her age ('woman, 22') — the only headlines to signal individual identity rather than anonymous casualty count. NDTV World is the sole outlet to foreground the crowd scale ('Attended By 3,500'), implicitly framing this as a mass public-safety incident rather than a discrete crime. AFP/France 24 EN is the only outlet to personalize the perpetrator with 'Gunman', while all peers use the passive-construction 'shooting'.
event_summary: A 22-year-old woman was killed and five others injured in a shooting at a rave in Aarau, Switzerland, shortly after 2:30 a.m. on 30 August 2026; police launched a large-scale manhunt with the perpetrators' identities and motives unknown.

evidence.quote: Gunman kills one at Swiss rave party
1 killed as shooting erupts at rave party in Switzerland
woman, 22, shot dead and five people wounded at rave

single_outlet_findings.finding: The only headline in the corpus to use the word 'Gunman' — 'Gunman kills one at Swiss rave party' — personalizing the perpetrator as a human actor rather than the impersonal 'shooting' used by all other outlets. This is the most agent-centered headline in the corpus, foregrounding culpability rather than event.

Only outlet to foreground event scale at title level — '1 Dead, 5 Injured In Shooting Near Rave Attended By 3,500 In Switzerland' — implicitly framing this as a mass public-safety incident. Every other outlet omits crowd size from the headline entirely, treating this as a discrete crime rather than a mass public gathering disrupted.

One of only two outlets (with Daily Mail) to humanize the victim with gender and age in the headline — 'kills woman, 22' — shifting from anonymous casualty count to individualized victim identity. All other outlets render the dead as 'one person,' '1 dead,' or 'one killed' without demographic specifics.

bottom_line: The headline layer reduces this story to its most essential criminal facts — a fatal shooting at a Swiss rave, one dead, five injured, perpetrators unknown — with all 22 outlets publishing manhunt or shooting-event headlines and no title addressing motive, gun policy, or security doctrine; the SECURITY_DEFENSE mobilisation frame and HEALTH_SAFETY casualty framing present in body text are entirely absent at headline level, a substantial body-versus-headline gap the divergence-index should capture.
